A1.justification: Despite the changed title and method names, both PDFs describe the same research, with matching algorithms and proof appendices. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Cityscapes experiments, gradient-norm versus smoothness observations, and runtime measurements in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains the original Cityscapes experiments and runtime measurements and adds NYU-v2 results in Table 2.

M1.justification: GSMGrad, SGSMGrad and GSMGrad-FA are renamed as MGDA variants. Equations (5)–(6) and Algorithms 1–4 retain the regularized weight updates, double sampling, optional warm start and fast approximation. The explicit warm-start options clarify an existing distinction rather than change the procedure.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates Cityscapes segmentation and depth estimation. v4 retains these and adds NYU-v2 with 13-class segmentation, depth estimation and surface-normal estimation, substantially extending dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The Cityscapes comparison replaces SDMGrad with FAMO. The added NYU-v2 comparison also includes LS, SI, RLW, DWA and UW, which were absent from v3's empirical comparisons. These expand the comparator set beyond merely extending existing baselines to another dataset.

E3.justification: The new NYU-v2 evaluation introduces mean and median angular errors, percentages within 11.25, 22.5 and 30 degrees, and an MR column. The documented Cityscapes protocol remains unchanged, including 200 epochs, batch size 8 and averaging test performance over the last 10 epochs.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same gradient-norm versus smoothness analyses and fast-approximation accuracy/runtime comparison. Moving Figure 1 and combining existing measurements in Appendix A.2 do not add analyses. No new ablation, sensitivity or robustness study is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging performance over the last 10 epochs and runtime over epochs is retained unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 adds the NYU-v2 result table, including Delta-m values of -4.42 for MGDA-warm start and -4.10 for FAMO. It adds FAMO's Cityscapes result of 8.13 and removes SDMGrad's 7.79 row. Matched Cityscapes scores and runtimes remain unchanged; the fast-approximation scores are retained in Appendix A.2.

T1.justification: Table 1 adds an explicit multi-task-curvature definition and additional comparator assumptions. Section 5.1 also corrects the sample-complexity typo from O(epsilon^11) to O(epsilon^-11). The paper's own substantive assumptions, convergence guarantees and detailed proofs in Appendices C–D remain unchanged; other theorem edits mainly clarify bound notation.

C1.justification: v3 presents newly proposed GSMGrad and SGSMGrad algorithms as central contributions. v4's title, abstract, contributions and conclusion instead center on proving convergence of fundamental MGDA and its stochastic variant under generalized smoothness. This substantially redefines the claimed contribution while retaining the convergence orders and CA-distance guarantees.

C2.justification: v4 newly justifies excluding SDMGrad because of its preference-based regularization and suggests that the analysis and warm-start strategy could benefit other MOO algorithms. Existing explanations of CA-distance control and the smoothness observations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the same SGD training procedure, hyperparameter search and selected values, NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware, and smoothness-illustration settings. The added NYU-v2 results are not accompanied by dedicated implementation or training details.

R1.justification: The work is repositioned from proposing new optimizers to analyzing established MGDA machinery. Table 1 replaces the stochastic complexity comparison with a broader deterministic/stochastic assumption comparison, adding CAGrad and PCGrad assumptions and explaining the original MGDA omission. Four references are added, covering random weighting, multi-task attention, NYU-v2 and generalized-smooth RMSProp/Adam.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivating introduction, contribution list, algorithm descriptions and conclusion are substantially rewritten around MGDA convergence. Terminology changes throughout, and the introduction gains an explicit research question. The overall section sequence and proof-appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 redesigns Table 1, adds the NYU-v2 table, enlarges and reorganizes the Cityscapes comparison, and combines retained accuracy and runtime results in Appendix Table 4. Figure 1 moves into the introduction, and algorithm boxes gain explicit option annotations. The plotted observations themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: NYU-v2 provides useful evidence that task balancing extends beyond the original two-task experiment to three objectives including surface normals. The revised assumption table and combined accuracy/runtime table also make scope and tradeoffs easier to assess. These are limited gains: the proofs and matched results are unchanged, NYU-v2 lacks dedicated implementation and uncertainty details, and the SDMGrad empirical comparison is removed.
